sentences.text:
Applicant :- Yogesh Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Ajay Kumar Dwivedi,Ajay Kumar Pandey,Deepak Singh,Mayank Awasth Counsel for Opposite Party :- Anita Singh,G.A.,Prem Babu Verma Hon'ble Subhash Chandra Sharma,J.
Supplementary affidavit filed today by learned counsel for the applicant is taken on record.

Heard Sri Satish Trivedi learned Senior counsel assisted by Mr Ajay Kumar Pandey and Mr Mayank Awasthi learned counsel for the applicant, Mrs Anita Singh learned counsel for the opposite party as well as learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material on record.
This bail application has been filed with a prayer to allow this bail application and release the applicant on bail in Case Crime No. 214 of 2019, under Sections 498A, 304-B I.P.C. and 3/4 D.P.
Act, Police Station Mirhachi, District Etah during the pendency of trial.

Yogesh vs State Of U.P. on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57120093/
1
It is submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that in this case applicant is husband of the deceased.

It is further submitted that though the death of the deceased took place after two years of her marriage on account of ante-mortem injuries found on her person including throttling but it was not done by the applicant himself.

It is further submitted that applicant was outside his home when the incident took place but after her death F.I.R. was lodged and he was sent to jail that was the reason he could not make pairvi in the case.

It is also submitted that applicant is languishing in jail for five years and there are two children at home and no other person is there to look after them,
therefore, request to release him on bail during the pendency of trial.
Learned counsel for the opposite party as well as learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer as aforesaid.

On considering the submissions made by learned counsel for both the parties as well as learned A.G.A. and perusal of record, the post-mortem report, it appears that the deceased was married with the applicant about three years prior to the alleged incident when she was found dead in the house of the applicant.

The deceased was aged about 22 years and in post-mortem report there were eight ante-mortem injuries on her person and cause of death was throttling which shows that she did not commit suicide but her death was homicidal.
In view of aforesaid facts, there appears no ground to grant bail in favour of the applicant.
Accordingly, this bail application is, hereby, rejected.

However, the learned trial court is directed to make its endeavor to conclude the trial as expeditiously as possible within a period of one year from the date of production of certified copy of this order.

Order Date :- 12.8.2024 Suraj Srivastav  Yogesh vs State Of U.P. on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57120093/
